title: How AI search is changing what people type before they buy
excerpt: For years, search marketing trained us to think in keywords. Someone wanted an accountant, running shoes or project management software, so they typed a short phrase into Google.
content:
For years, search marketing trained us to think in keywords. Someone wanted an accountant, running shoes or project management software, so they typed a short phrase into Google.

That behaviour is not disappearing. But artificial intelligence is giving people another way to search before they buy.

Instead of typing "best CRM small business", a buyer can ask: "What CRM is best for a 15-person professional services firm that needs HubSpot integration, simple reporting and no long implementation?"

That search contains the category, company type, technical requirement, buying concern and desired outcome in one query.

This is where AI Overview and AI Mode start to matter for marketers. Search is becoming better at handling the way people naturally explain a problem, so the language used before a purchase can become longer, more specific and more conversational.

Search is moving from keywords towards briefs

Google's May 2026 U.S. data gives us a useful signal. The company says the average AI Mode query is three times the length of a traditional Search query. It also reports faster growth in planning, brainstorming and "where should I" style searches inside AI Mode.

That does not mean short searches are finished. It means a search engine can handle more context without forcing users to translate a real problem into a neat keyword.

A buyer once had to split research across several searches. With generative AI in Search, questions can increasingly be combined with a budget, workflow, preferences and constraints, followed by another question without starting again.

The query starts to look less like a keyword and more like a buying brief.

AI Overview changes what happens before the click

An AI Overview is a Google Search feature that can provide an AI-generated snapshot on the search results page, with links for further exploration. Google also now lets users move from an AI Overview into a follow-up conversation in AI Mode while retaining the context of the original search.

A buyer may therefore receive a summary of a category, important considerations and relevant sources before visiting a website.

For businesses, that means the first website visit may happen later in the decision process. A potential customer can arrive already knowing the basic options and asking a narrower question.

Your content therefore has to do more than define the category. It needs to help someone evaluate a decision.

Commercial searches can contain more conditions

Traditional keyword research groups demand around a product or service plus modifiers such as "best", "price", "reviews" or "near me".

Those modifiers still matter, but AI search makes it easier to express several conditions at once.

Someone looking for an agency might ask for a partner that works with B2B companies, understands a particular market, can handle strategy and production, has experience with a specific platform and works within a defined budget.

The commercial intent is not weaker because the query is longer. The extra detail often tells you more about what stands between the buyer and the purchase.

That is useful information for content strategy.

What should businesses publish for AI search?

The answer is not hundreds of pages written for robots.

Google's guidance is that the same fundamental SEO practices apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode. There are no additional technical requirements or secret AI optimisation method required simply because the search result is generated with artificial intelligence.

Useful content still needs to be crawlable, indexable and understandable. Important information should exist in text, internal links should make pages easy to discover, and structured data should accurately match the visible page.

So the opportunity is mostly editorial.

A strong product or service page should explain who the offer is for, what problem it solves, how pricing works, what alternatives exist, what the process involves and what evidence supports the claims.

A useful article should answer a real decision question rather than stretch one keyword across 1,500 words.

Query fan-out changes the content opportunity

AI Mode and AI Overviews can use what Google calls "query fan-out". The system can run multiple related searches across subtopics and data sources before building a response. Google describes this as a way to answer nuanced questions that might previously have required several separate searches.

That matters because one complex buying question may contain several smaller questions.

If someone asks for the best website platform for an Irish professional services business that needs strong SEO, easy editing and fast performance, Google may need information about platforms, SEO capabilities, content management, performance and business type.

One page does not need to rank for every possible phrase. But a website should build a coherent body of useful information around the decisions its customers actually make.

This is where topic depth becomes more useful than keyword repetition.

The buying journey is becoming less linear

People still discover, compare, validate and buy. What changes is how many of those stages can happen inside one search session.

A person can move from "What are my options?" to "Which is better for my situation?" to "What should I watch out for?" without repeating the context each time.

Generic awareness content therefore has to earn its place. If an AI feature can answer the basic definition instantly, your page needs another reason to be visited. Original expertise, examples, clear comparisons, evidence and practical detail become more valuable.

Conversion content also needs to anticipate a better-informed visitor. The person arriving on your website may be looking for proof rather than an introduction.

What should you measure?

Rankings still matter, but compare them with qualified enquiries, demo requests, calls or sales. Watch the queries bringing people to your site, which pages assist conversions and whether your brand appears in AI-generated search experiences where customers research your category.

Measurement is still evolving, so no single visibility tool should be treated as perfect.

Frequently asked questions

What is an AI Overview?

An AI Overview is an AI-generated snapshot that can appear in Google Search when Google's systems determine a generative response could be useful. It can summarise information and provide links to supporting web sources.

Are keywords becoming irrelevant?

No. Keywords still describe categories, products, services and demand. What is changing is that users can express more context around those keywords, making detailed and conversational searches more practical.

Build for the question behind the keyword

The biggest change in AI search is not that people stop using keywords. It is that they no longer have to compress every buying problem into two or three words.

For marketers, that means search strategy is not simply about finding more phrases to target. It is about understanding what customers need to know before they are comfortable buying and creating content that answers those questions clearly.
